title: Optical Mapping of Action Potentials and Calcium Transients in the Mouse Heart
protocol: Prepare two stock solutions of Tyrode's solution in advance in deionized water and store them at 4°C: Stock I (119.872 g/L NaCl, 3.056 g/L CaCl2 (2H2O), 5.6 g/L KCl, 2.6274 g/L NaH2PO4, 3.408 g/L MgCl2 (6H2O)); Stock II (26.88 g/L NaHCO3).
Store 30 μl aliquots of voltage-sensitive dye RH237 stock solution at -20°C.
Store 30 μl aliquots of calcium indicator Rhod-2AM stock solution at -20°C.
Prepare excitation-contraction uncoupler blebbistatin stock solution (2 mg/mL in DMSO) and store the dissolved blebbistatin at 4°C.
Freshly prepare 2L Tyrode's solution by mixing 1750 mL of deionized water with 125 mL of Stock I, 125 mL of Stock II, and 4g of glucose.
Turn on the two pumps of the perfusion systems.
Set the peristaltic pump for retrograde perfusion to 40 mL/min.
Set the other peristaltic pump for superfusion and returning perfusate back to the holding reservoir to 80 mL/min.
Wash the perfusion system with 70% ethanol for 30 min.
Wash the perfusion system with 2L deionized water.
Evacuate all deionized water from the chamber.
Circulate Tyrode's solution through a 5-μm filter.
Warm the perfusate to +37°C using a water jacket and circulator.
Oxygenate the perfusate by bubbling O2/CO2 (95% / 5%) gas into the solution.
Monitor the pH of the solution with a pH meter.
Adjust the rate of O2/CO2 bubbling to maintain the pH at 7.35 ± .05.
Continue monitoring pH and temperature during the experiment.
Fix a band-pass filter (590±15 nm) in front of the designated calcium imaging camera.
Position a long-pass filter (>700 nm) in front of the designated voltage imaging camera.
Arrange two MiCAM Ultima-L CMOS cameras perpendicular to one another by a holder containing a dichroic mirror (635 nm cutoff).
Place a lens focusing emission light from the heart onto the dichroic mirror below the dual camera holder.
Prepare Ag/AgCl2 electrodes for pacing and sensing in advance.
Install prepared electrodes in the chamber prior to placing the heart.
Adjust amplifiers and filters to appropriate levels.
Anesthetize the mouse with ketamine/xylazine (ketamin, 80 mg/kg bodyweight; xylazine, 10 mg/kg bodyweight) and heparin (100 units) by intraperitoneal injection.
Assure appropriate level of anesthesia by checking the lack of pain reflex.
Make a mid-sternal incision to quickly remove the heart.
Wash the heart in oxygenated Tyrode's solution at 37±1°C.
Identify the aorta and make a clean cut across the ascending aorta below the right subclavian artery.
Attach a short section of aorta to a custom-made 21-gauge cannula with a flared tip.
Fix the heart onto the cannula using 4-0 black-braided silk suture.
Retrogradely perfuse and superfuse the heart with Tyrode's solution.
Adjust the retrograde perfusion rate in the range of 2-5 mL/min to maintain aortic pressure between 60 and 80 mmHg.
Dissect and remove lung, thymus, and fat tissue after cannulation.
Pin the isolated heart at the apex to the bottom of the perfusion chamber.
Stretch and pin the right atrial appendage to the bottom of the chamber.
Stretch and pin the left atrial appendage to the bottom of the chamber.
Insert a small silicon tube into the left ventricle through the pulmonary veins.
Fix the silicon tube by silk suture to nearby connective tissue.
Place a custom-made electrode on the surface of the heart for pacing stimulations.
Generate pacing stimulations using Master-8 or PowerLab 26T.
Fix a small cover glass on the surface of the solution over the heart.
Focus the excitation light on the heart.
Adjust the distance between the dual camera apparatus and the heart for maximum resolution.
Turn off all lights in the room.
Commence electrical recordings using PowerLab 26T.
Warm up 0.6 mL of blebbistatin.
Mix 0.5 mL of the blebbistatin with the perfusate in the holding reservoir.
Dilute the remaining 0.1 mL of blebbistatin in 1 mL of Tyrode's solution and slowly inject it through a drug port near the cannula over a 20-minute period.
Mix 30 μL of voltage-sensitive dye RH237 stock solution with 1 mL Tyrode's solution and slowly inject into the same injection port as blebbistatin over 5-7 minutes.
Mix 30 μL calcium indicator Rhod-2 AM with Pluronic F127 (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, 20% solution in DMSO) at a ratio of 1:1 and then dilute it in 1 mL Tyrode's solution.
Slowly apply the diluted Rhod-2 AM over 5-10 minutes through the same injection port as blebbistatin.
Wait for 5-10 minutes for blebbistatin and dyes to reach the cell membrane and cytosol.
Continue with the protocol when motion is completely suppressed.
Continuously monitor ECG recordings throughout the procedure to ensure normal electrical function of the heart.
Commence fluorescent signal recordings using SciMedia custom software (SciMedia, Costa Mesa, CA).
